claim_1.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of sera from 56 vaccinated individuals showed robust production of neutralizing antibodies against the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 and, to a lesser extent, the B.1.351 strain after secondary vaccination compared to primary vaccination.

sources.quote: Vaccination resulted in the robust production of neutralizing antibodies against the wild-type SARS-CoV-2 (derived from 2019-nCOV/USA_WA1/2020) and, to a lesser extent, the B.1.351 strain, as well as significant increases in antigen-specific polyfunctional CD4 and CD8 T cells after the second dose.

claim_2.claim: CyTOF analysis of whole-blood samples from 27 vaccinated individuals showed increased frequency of intermediate monocytes two days after the primary vaccination (day 2) and substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination (day 23) compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14 + CD16 + monocytes) increased significantly two days after the primary vaccination, and was substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination ( Fig. 2b ).

claim_3.claim: Olink assay of plasma from 31 vaccinated individuals showed significant increases in IFNγ and CXCL10 concentrations on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination (days 1 and 2) and further increases after secondary immunization (days 22 and 23).

sources.quote: Of the 67 cytokines detected, the concentration of 2 cytokines (IFNγ and CXCL10) were increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination ( Fig. 2e left). Similar to our observations on intermediate monocytes and pSTAT1 and pSTAT3, the concentrations of these cytokines were increased even further after the secondary immunization ( Fig. 2e right).

claim_4.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole blood from 31 participants showed a fourfold increase in differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1, with secondary vaccination leading to increases in signatures of dendritic cell activation and upregulation of Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte, and neutrophil modules.

sources.quote: Secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response (as has previously been seen in a recent study of adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccine 17 ), with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 as compared to day 1 ( Fig. 3a ); this is consistent with the increased markers of innate immunity detected by both CyTOF and Olink ( Fig. 2 ).

claim_5.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from 6 individuals showed the emergence of cluster C8, which expressed interferon-stimulated genes and increased almost 100-fold to about 1% one day after secondary vaccination (day 22) compared to day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1).

sources.quote: Notably, cluster C8 (which expressed CD14 , VCAN , CD1C , FCGR1A and CD274 mRNA or protein) emerged on day 22, one day after secondary vaccination ( Fig. 4b ). These cells uniquely expressed interferon-stimulated genes, including WARS (also known as WARS1 ), GBP1 , IFI30 and IFITM3 , and constituted about 0.01% of the Lin − HLA-DR + population on day 1 after primary vaccination but increased almost 100-fold to about 1% one day after secondary vaccination ( Fig. 4c ).
